task.title: Stop the board columns from self-scrolling on every poll
task.description:
A status column that a user has scrolled creeps further down on its own with every one-second poll, and reaches the bottom of the column without anyone touching it. Reported 2026-08-06; reproduced and root-caused the same day at commit c453596.

## Reproduction

Served the projects own board and drove real Chrome 151 headless over CDP. The DONE column held 37 tasks (clientHeight 635, scrollHeight 9189). Scrolled it to 35 percent, then sampled scrollTop once per poll:

  t+1.1s 3145   t+2.2s 3221   t+3.3s 3297   t+4.4s 3373   t+5.5s 3466
  t+6.6s 3559   t+7.7s 3635   t+8.8s 3729   t+9.9s 3823   t+11.0s 3916

Monotonic, about 76 to 93 px per tick, roughly a third of a card height. Nothing was interacting with the page. Left alone it walks to the bottom and stays there.

## Root cause

Browser scroll anchoring, triggered by wholesale DOM replacement on every render.

render() rebuilds each column from scratch on every poll: it builds a fresh DocumentFragment of new card nodes and calls list.replaceChildren(fragment) (internal/webui/assets/index.html:1806-1808), driven by window.setInterval(refresh, 1000) at index.html:1957. Every card node in every column is destroyed and recreated once a second, whether or not anything changed.

.task-list is a scroll container (display grid with overflow-y auto, index.html:46) and nothing sets overflow-anchor anywhere in the stylesheet, so the browser default of auto applies and scroll anchoring is active. Confirmed at runtime: getComputedStyle(list).overflowAnchor === "auto".

Each tick the anchor node the browser selected is destroyed along with everything else. Anchoring then re-selects against entirely new nodes and applies a positive scroll adjustment, so the position ratchets downward once per second.

Worth correcting the original theory: the client has no scroll-position tracking to get wrong. The only scroll code in the whole client is combobox positioning (index.html:663, 669) and a scrollIntoView for keyboard navigation (:734). Nothing attempts to save or restore column scroll, so this is the browser compensating for churn rather than the app miscalculating.

## Evidence

Three controlled runs, same page and same column:

1. Mechanism. Default anchoring drifted 2994 to 3578 over 8 ticks (delta 584). Setting overflow-anchor none on .task-list held 2994 across all 8 ticks (delta 0). Anchoring is the mechanism.
2. Trigger. With the pages own polling frozen and no DOM edits at all, scrollTop held exactly at 2994: nothing ambient moves it. Calling replaceChildren with byte-identical clones of the existing cards, so the data did not change and only node identity did, drifted 2994 to 3466 over 6 iterations (delta 472). Node-identity churn alone is sufficient; changed data is not required.
3. Node reuse. Editing text in place on the existing nodes produced a single 36 px adjustment for the real layout change and then held at 3030 across five further iterations. That is anchoring behaving correctly. Preserving node identity removes the per-tick ratchet.

## Fix

Two independent fixes, and they address different levels.

Reconcile instead of replacing, which is the root cause fix. Diff the incoming task list against what is rendered, keyed by task ID, and only create, remove, move, or update what actually changed. Evidence item 3 shows this eliminates the ratchet. It also removes a standing waste: all 65 cards are currently rebuilt 60 times a minute for as long as the tab is open, almost always producing an identical DOM. That churn is also why the is-refreshing opacity flash at index.html:47 and 1809 exists at all, and reconciliation may let it go away.

Set overflow-anchor none on .task-list, which is one line and proven to fully stop the drift. Reasonable as an immediate mitigation, and defensible to keep afterwards as a guard, but on its own it leaves the churn in place.

Recommend doing the reconciliation and keeping the CSS declaration as a belt-and-braces guard, since any future code path that rebuilds a column would otherwise reintroduce this silently.

## Acceptance

- A column scrolled to an arbitrary position holds that position across at least ten consecutive polls with no user interaction.
- A poll that genuinely changes a columns contents still updates it, and does not reset an unrelated columns scroll position to the top.
- Cards that did not change are not recreated; verify by holding a node reference across a poll and asserting it is still connected.
- Scroll position survives a card being added to or removed from another column.
- Regression coverage. The existing client tests run in a fake DOM with no layout, so they cannot observe this. Either add a real-browser check, or assert the reconciliation contract directly, that an unchanged task keeps its node identity across a render, which is the property whose absence causes the bug and is testable in the existing harness.

Note the existing handler_test.go references at :1013-1023 to top, middle, and bottom scroll position are combobox placement cases, not board scrolling, so nothing here is covered today.

## Related

The reconciliation work overlaps the optimistic mutation queue, which projects pending intents over polled task state and re-renders through this same path. Coordinate with the queue lost-update ticket so the render path is restructured once rather than twice.
